newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Yeltsin's cabinet moves.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Yeltsin's cabinet moves.

text.p: The United States, declaring that "Boris Yeltsin is back", welcomed on Tuesday the first appointments in the Russian president's cabinet reshuffle as a sign that reforms would continue.

"The fact that he has retained Prime Minister (Viktor) Chernomyrdin and First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais means one thing -- Russia continues to be headed in a reform direction," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

A presidential decree published by Yeltsin's press service on Tuesday ordered Chernomyrdin to come up with cabinet proposals within a week. Itar-Tass news agency said Yeltsin may announce the changes by the end of this week.
Analysts said that Chubais, a former privatisation chief who was dropped from the cabinet last year then brought back last Friday, would be the driving force behind the changes.

Burns told a news briefing that Yeltsin, who has been handicapped for months by bouts with heart disease and pneumonia, had "very firmly reasserted his control" in a state of the union speech last week.
"He asserted a very strong and coherent and forcefully delivered view on the domestic priorities of the Russian Federation and on Russian foreign policy," Burns said.

"President Yeltsin is back. President Yeltsin has firm control of the Russian government ... There's no question that what we've seen over the last two weeks is a resurgent, very forceful, reform-minded President Boris Yeltsin."

The apparent improvement in Yeltsin's health could hardly have come at a better time for the United States, with President Bill Clinton due to meet the Russian leader at a Helsinki summit March 19-20.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov is due in Washington on Saturday to prepare the summit agenda. He meets Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Saturday and Clinton on Monday.
